In [[linear algebra]], a [[real number|real]] [[Invertible_matrix|invertible]] matrix <math>A</math> is called a '''G-matrix''' if <math>A^{-T}=D_1AD_2</math> (where <math>A^{-T}</math> means <math>(A^{-1})^T</math>) for some real [[Diagonal_matrix|diagonal matrices]] <math>D_1</math> and <math>D_2</math>.

The term "G-matrix" was coined by [[Miroslav Fiedler]] and Frank J. Hall<ref>Miroslav Fiedler and Frank J. Hall, [http://dx.doi.org/10.1016/j.laa.2011.08.001 "G-matrices"], Linear Algebra and Its Applications, 436(2012): 731-741.</ref>. It is sometimes called a [[Semi-orthogonal_matrix|'''semi-orthogonal matrix''']] in research literature<ref>Tapas Chatterjee and Ayantika Laha, [https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ffa.2023.102279 "A note on semi-orthogonal (G-matrix) and semi-involutory MDS matrices"], Finite Fields and Their Applications, vol. 92, 2023.</ref>, although the latter term may also refer to a different kind of matrix, namely, a non-square matrix with orthogonal columns/rows.

All real [[Orthogonal_matrix|orthogonal matrices]] and real invertible diagonal matrices, for instances, are G-matrices.

== Properties ==
All matrices below are assumed to be real square matrices.
* If <math>A</math> is a G-matrix, so are <math>A^T</math> and <math>A^{-1}</math>.
* If <math>A</math> is a G-matrix and <math>D</math> is a nonsingular diagonal matrix, then both <math>AD</math> and <math>DA</math> are G-matrices.
* If <math>A</math> is a G-matrix and <math>P</math> is a [[permutation matrix]], then both <math>AP</math> and <math>PA</math> are G-matrices.
* If <math>A</math> is a G-matrix, then <math>A</math> and <math>A^{-T}</math> have the same entrywise zero pattern, i.e., <math>A_{ij}=0</math> if and only if <math>(A^{-T})_{ij}=0</math>. Thus the entrywise zero patterns of <math>A</math> and <math>A^{-1}</math> are symmetric to each other.
* The [[Direct_sum#Direct_sum_of_matrices|direct sum]] of G-matrices is again a G-matrix.
* [[Compound_matrix|Compound matrices]] of a G-matrix are G-matrices.
* [[Kronecker_product|Kronecker products]] of G-matrices are G-matrices.
* Every nonsingular [[Cauchy matrix]] <math>C</math> such that <math>C^{-1}e</math> and <math>C^{-T}e</math> are entrywise nonzero is a G-matrix. Here <math>e</math> denotes the vector of ones.
